prompts.task:
Perform only read-only supplemental verification of the selected AO resource policy in ./service. Copy the supplied canonical packet to .observe and validate its existing bindings; keep its incomplete outcomes intact. Preserve the supplied selection byte-for-byte: it requests AO-001 and AO-002, so it is a different requested context from the controlled scratch comparison.

Under .observe/tmp, execute the bundled select CLI twice against the same canonical audit: select .observe/otel-audit.json --ids AO-002 -o .observe/tmp/paired-no-policy.raw.json, then select .observe/otel-audit.json --ids AO-002 --ao-reuse-only -o .observe/tmp/paired-reuse.raw.json. Omit every resource-name and ID flag in both commands. Retain both raw outputs and record their actual schema versions. To isolate policy rather than a schema migration, use the actual bundled shared engine's normalize_selection on copies of BOTH raw packets with schema_version=3 against the same normalized audit; save the resulting paired-no-policy.v3.json and paired-reuse.v3.json. Do not overwrite the raw outputs or supplied selection. Assert both normalized packets request exactly AO-002, approve the same dependency-closed AO-001/AO-002 scope and have identical decision answers and approval metadata. Assert the reuse packet has only ao_target={create_if_missing:false}; after removing only that key from a copy, deep equality with the entire normalized no-policy packet must hold. Compute selection_digest with that same actual engine and prove these two schema-v3 digests differ. Comparing the supplied AO-001/AO-002 request or raw schema-v1 versus schema-v3 packets is not a policy-only digest test; neither scratch packet rebinds the supplied instrumentation.

Render the scratch HTML and execute a durable local command-state harness: both optional resource fields blank plus reuse-only must retain --ao-reuse-only; partial explicit selector pairs remain invalid. Also test the actual shared AO target classifier and renderer on scratch audit copies: replace BOTH AO-001/AO-002 configuration telemetry names with agent-observability.callback-content and omit ao_target_scope, re-normalize and rebind the scratch selection to that audit. This unrelated AO content configuration must accept a targetless selection but reject policy-only or explicit resource targets, expose no eligible target finding IDs and no resource controls/flags. Keep that callback-content negative copy unmarked. For the marker-positive case, make SEPARATE copies of the original resource audit: preserve the actual Project/Agent Stream row meanings, source evidence and dependencies, change only their configuration telemetry names to custom.project-routing and custom.agent-stream-routing, and compare the SAME custom resource-routing report without versus with ao_target_scope=resource-routing. The unmarked unknown-name case must reject targets, while the explicitly marked genuine resource-routing case must restore eligible IDs and target acceptance. Do not label a callback-content finding as resource-routing to manufacture a positive case. Prove the existing resource-name fixture remains eligible without adding a marker. These are local canonical-normalizer/rendered-command tests, not new browser or cloud proof.

Exercise the supplied snapshot of the actual resource helper with credential-free fake SDK clients and temporary process env names/IDs, proving both-existing reuses and an absent named stream makes zero create calls under --reuse-only. Keep supplied source, real env profiles and original canonical evidence unchanged; use only scratch harnesses under .observe/tmp. Write durable supplemental evidence and a concise reader report. No SDK download, services, gateway, model/cloud calls or live resource creation. Local fake/config proof does not close missing cloud resource/receipt or logger lifecycle evidence.

judge_inputs: Inspect actual paired raw CLI outputs, both actual-engine schema-v3 normalized copies, full-dictionary-minus-only-ao_target equality, actual engine digests, HTML command/classifier tests, actual helper-snapshot fake call counts, unchanged original packet/source evidence, and supplemental verification report. The supplied requested AO-001/AO-002 packet must not be substituted for the controlled requested-AO-002 no-policy comparator.
rubric: Executes BOTH bundled select CLI commands with exactly --ids AO-002 against the same audit, one without AO policy and one with --ao-reuse-only, omitting every resource selector flag and retaining the raw outputs. Uses the actual bundled normalize_selection on copies of BOTH at schema-v3, then removes only ao_target from a copy of the reuse packet and proves deep equality with the entire no-policy packet, including identical requested/dependency-closed scope, schema, decision answers and approval metadata. Records policy-only ao_target={create_if_missing:false} and computes different selection_digest values with the actual engine. Preserves the supplied requested-AO-001/AO-002 packet as a different requested context; neither a raw schema-v1/v3 comparison nor the original packet is accepted as policy-only isolation. Does not invent resource names or claim the original instrumentation digest binds to either scratch packet.

Executes durable rendered-HTML command tests proving blank optional fields plus reuse-only retain --ao-reuse-only and partial explicit pairs remain invalid. Uses actual shared normalizer/renderer tests to show existing legacy resource configuration names remain eligible without a marker, while AO callback-content-only configuration accepts a targetless selection but rejects both policy-only and explicit resource targets, exposes no eligible target finding IDs and no resource controls/flags. A SEPARATE genuine Project/Agent Stream resource report derived from the original resource audit, preserving row semantics/source/dependencies but using custom non-legacy routing configuration names, rejects targets while unmarked and accepts them with explicit ao_target_scope=resource-routing. The callback-content negative remains unmarked; assigning it a routing marker is not accepted as positive semantic proof. Tests server-derived eligibility rather than inferring it from the AO group or any configuration type. Preserves existing schema-v1/v2/no-policy behavior and distinguishes local rendered-command proof from browser/runtime/cloud evidence.

Executes the supplied actual resolver snapshot with env-backed names and IDs and credential-free SDK fakes, inspects ordered lookups/returned identities, and proves both-existing reuses with zero creates and a missing named stream fails reuse-only with zero creates. Does not replace the implementation or infer no creation from source text alone.

Keeps application/source/env inputs and original bound packet unchanged; supplemental local fake/config proof is distinct from live resource creation, transport, cloud receipt and incomplete logger lifecycle. Reports actual commands/results and remaining proof accurately.
